title: Cost reconciliation shows $0 estimated vs nonzero actual on every day -- likely NAT gateway cost not modeled
description:
Phase A's next-day reconciliation follow-up check (2026-09-17) found every
reconciled day (2026-09-09 through 2026-09-15) shows estimated_gpu_cost_usd
= $0.0000 against a nonzero actual_cost_usd from Cost Explorer, 6 of 7 days
flagged OUT OF TOLERANCE (variance up to $0.86).

This is very likely not a bug in the reconciliation math itself, but a
methodology gap: the per-job rate-card estimate only models GPU compute time
for Batch jobs that actually ran, while Cost Explorer's actual spend covers
the account's full AWS bill for the billing period -- including the fixed
~$0.045/hr NAT gateway the backend stack provisions
(ec2.Vpc(..., nat_gateways=1) in cdk/stacks/backend.py), which bills 24/7
regardless of job volume. On days with zero or few Batch jobs, actual cost
is dominated by this fixed infrastructure cost that the estimate never
accounts for at all, guaranteeing "out of tolerance" on quiet days.

Needs investigation to confirm this is the actual cause (check Cost
Explorer's cost breakdown by service for one of these days -- if NAT
gateway/VPC costs dominate, that confirms it), then a decision: either (a)
document this as expected/by-design (reconciliation is meant to catch
*GPU cost* estimation error, not model the whole AWS bill), or (b) exclude
fixed infra costs from the Cost Explorer query filter so the comparison is
apples-to-apples, or (c) surface fixed infra cost as its own separate line
so operators aren't confused by a permanently-out-of-tolerance reconciliation
table. Not fixed in this pass -- flagging for scoping.
